definition: VGT3 is an Amazon facility in Las Vegas used for data harvesting and destructive book scanning to train large language models.
details: Employees at VGT3 receive the books, cut their spines, and scan their pages, destroying the books in the process.

explainer.lead: VGT3 is an Amazon facility in Las Vegas used for data harvesting and destructive book scanning to train large language models. It matters because it shows the physical, irreversible side of assembling training data.

tiers.eli5: Books go in, and they get their spines cut off so every page can be scanned into a computer; the books don't come back out.
tiers.practitioner: Staff receive books, cut their spines, and scan the pages, so any pipeline depending on this source is working from scans of destroyed originals. The pitfall is that the source material is consumed, not preserved.
tiers.paperLevel: A data-acquisition operation defined by a fixed procedure: receive books, cut spines, scan pages, destroying each book in the process. There is no formal model here; the limit is that scanning is one-way and the books are not retained.

explainer.example: A shipment of books arrives at the Las Vegas facility; employees cut the spine of each one and scan its pages, and the books are destroyed.
